line.text: Your couch. 1:12 AM. Her case notes are a neat stack on the floor now, squared off at the edges.
I should go. I have a deposition at nine and my suit is at my place, which is currently without water, which is administratively temporary.
She doesn't move. Her tail has curled around the edge of the cushion, holding on.
The water situation is administratively temporary. I keep saying that. It doesn't become less true.
I've been sleeping less. That's not a complaint, it's a data point. My apartment is quiet in a way that registers as absence.
You don't have to go yet.
That's the thing. I want to. Stay. I'm saying it without the wrapper. Don't go.
Her ears flatten, then slowly rise again. She is watching your face the way she watches a scene: for what's actually there.
I know what loss looks like. That doesn't make it easier to - anyway. I'm not asking you to fix anything. I'm asking you to not leave the room.

choice.prompt: She is looking at you, waiting.

reaction.text: Her tail uncurls and sways once, slow, like a metronome finding its tempo.
Okay. Okay. I don't know what to do when someone just. Stays.

options.text: You memorized my schedule. I noticed.

reaction.text: You remembered that. You didn't have to.
Her ears curl inward, hiding interest, and she doesn't correct them.

options.text: You're exhausted. Let me take care of you.

reaction.text: I'm not fragile. I'm tired. There's a difference, and I need you to know it.
She stands, smooths her cardigan. Perfect grammar. Complete sentences.

line.text: The room settles. The radiator ticks. She is still here, which is its own kind of answer.
I called a Jane Doe once. Jane. After someone I tried not to think about. It didn't work. I thought about her anyway.
I don't tell people that. I'm telling you. I think I trust you. I'm saying it.
Her tail wraps once around her own ankle, a small self-hold. She is not performing composure. She is just here.
You make it harder to leave. Anyway.

choice.prompt: The lamp is still on. She hasn't moved.

reaction.text: She sets her glasses on the arm of the couch, lens-side down. A deliberate, unguarded motion.
Okay. I'll stay. But I'm taking the left side. I sleep on the left side. It's a fixed variable.

options.text: Tell me about the case that got to you.

reaction.text: It was a kid. My age at the time. I became more precise after, not less. That's the whole story.
She breathes out. Slowly. Like she has been holding it since the deposition was scheduled.
You didn't flinch. Most people do. Thank you for not doing that.

options.text: I could come closer, if you want.

reaction.text: Don't. Not yet. I need to - I need to be the one who closes the distance. I'm not uncomfortable. I'm processing.
She stands, puts two steps between you. The radiator ticks. She is still here, which is something.

desc: She asks you not to go. Quiet and charged: she is direct about wanting you close, in her clinical way.
